subtitle: A rich, fairly hot beef curry with rice and naan, suited to diners who enjoy lingering chilli heat.
quickAnswer: Wetherspoons Beef Madras costs a typical {price}, contains {calories} kcal and comes with fragrant rice and soft naan bread. Prices vary by pub, with [Curry Club](/curry-club) pricing on Thursdays. The slow-cooked beef sits in a dark tomato, chilli and spice sauce, making this a choice for diners comfortable with fairly hot curries.

components.name: Slow-cooked beef
components.note: Tender chunks of beef give the curry its substantial texture, with long cooking producing a soft, melting bite.

components.name: Madras sauce
components.note: The dark sauce combines tomatoes, fiery chillies and earthy spices for a rich, intensely savoury flavour with lingering heat.

components.name: Fragrant rice
components.note: Fragrant rice accompanies the curry, giving you something to combine with the rich sauce and tender beef.

components.name: Soft naan bread

taste:
Beef Madras is rich, intensely savoury and fairly hot, with a chilli warmth that lingers after each mouthful. Slow cooking gives the beef a tender, melting texture rather than a firm bite. The dark sauce brings together tomatoes, fiery chillies and deep, earthy spices, so the flavour has depth as well as heat.

Fragrant rice and soft naan accompany the curry, giving you different textures to work through alongside the beef and sauce. It is served piping hot, making the overall experience distinctly warming. Choose it for a bold spice profile, not a gentle curry: the sustained chilli heat is central to this dish rather than a small finishing note.

Do not treat this short list as confirmation that other allergens are absent. Ask about the full plate, including rice and naan, rather than just the curry. Any agreed swaps or additions can change the allergens in your meal.

bestFor.text: Choose this curry if you enjoy a fairly hot sauce with a lasting chilli finish. Its rich, earthy flavour gives you more than heat alone.

bestFor.title: Tender beef fans
